caption:
The video captures the curved, padded interior of a cabin seen through a wide-angle lens, where many people in dark flight suits occupy the space. Ceiling panels and a bundled rope on the left wall stay fixed, so the motion belongs to the occupants. Several are already drifting between horizontal floating poses and crouched, grounded stances in the cabin.

In the right foreground, a reddish-haired woman lowers from a floating pose until her feet touch the floor, settling into a crouch while extending an arm forward across the cabin. Behind her, a blonde woman floats with one arm extended, descends to a crouched stance, then rises again into a floating pose. Along the right wall, a man remains crouched against the padded surface for some time before lifting into a tucked float.

In the center, a few occupants remain crouched or seated on the floor, one holding a phone, while at the far-right edge a seated observer becomes visible holding a white-and-red megaphone.
relations: Floating occupants move relative to the cabin while not in supporting contact with its floor or walls.
When feet or bodies contact the cabin, support and friction forces can change their relative motion and permit crouched postures.
Transitions between floating and supported poses should remain continuous, with contact occurring where bodies meet the cabin surfaces.
Holding a phone or megaphone does not itself determine whether an occupant floats or remains supported.
analysis:
1. Floating occupants move relative to the cabin while not in supporting contact with its floor or walls.
2. When feet or bodies contact the cabin, support and friction forces can change their relative motion and permit crouched postures.
3. Transitions between floating and supported poses should remain continuous, with contact occurring where bodies meet the cabin surfaces.
4. Holding a phone or megaphone does not itself determine whether an occupant floats or remains supported.
original_relations: Padded cabin walls provide frictionless surface for occupants to crouch or float without slipping.
Gravity enables controlled descent to floor, allowing crouched stances to stabilize against cabin’s curved interior.
Rope’s fixed position anchors visual reference, contrasting motion of drifting occupants against static environment.
Megaphone’s grip requires seated posture, maintaining contact with floor to prevent floating during vocal use.
method: Input-only causal correction of complete legacy reasoning; no sentence selection, no future video, no API
